name: Open Items
rows: FY2026: cash at June 30, 2026 · USD · Cash audit workpapers
DRAFT FOR THE CPA · not an audit report · no opinion · the CPA reviews and concludes

The bank's $700.00 annual treasury services fee for 2026 of January 2, 2026 was never recorded. Cash and book income are overstated by $700.00. Proposed adjustment: debit a bank charges expense (the trial balance has no such account yet), credit 100110 Cash. It is 5.8% of materiality and under performance materiality, so if the client declines to record it the CPA may pass it and list it on the summary of passed adjustments. The machine never posts.

Check 1043, $700.00, for warranty claim HC-WCL-03 of December 3, 2025, has never been presented and was 209 days old at June 30, past the bank's 180-day limit. The unit owner has not been paid, yet the books count the claim as paid. Ask Morgan Lee to contact the unit owner and reissue it or void it with a stop payment. If voided: debit 100110 Cash, credit 220510 Warranty liability (or an unclaimed property liability). Cash rises by the same amount the bank charge lowers it.

The bank confirmed $42,300.00; the request showed the books' $29,900.00. The $12,400.00 difference is explained in full: 4 June payments that cleared July 1 and July 2 ($12,400.00), plus check 1043 ($700.00), less the unrecorded bank charge ($700.00). No adjustment beyond FEE-01 and STALE-01. The CPA accepts the explanation or asks for more.

The June 30 reconciliation was prepared by Morgan Lee on July 9, 2026 and no one has signed it as reviewed. It carried a bank charge for six months instead of recording it, and a stale check without follow-up. Ask who reviews the reconciliation each month; the CPA weighs it as a control observation.
The FY2026 trial balance export is marked “draft and unapproved”. Every figure here rests on it. Ask Morgan Lee for the approved version and compare its cash with this one.

Materiality is proposed at $12,000.00, 5% of book income, with performance materiality $9,000.00 and clearly trivial $600.00, the same as the year-end audit. The engagement partner sets the final amounts.
No management representation letter has been obtained. The CPA requests it near the end of fieldwork, including that every bank account has been disclosed.
These are draft workpapers and findings for the engagement partner. They are not an audit report and give no opinion. Nothing has been signed, posted or sent to the client or the bank.
